macroNarrative: Markets open Monday under a convergence of pressures: Brent crude holding near $109 on persistent US-Iran combat fears, the rupee having breached 96/USD before RBI intervention, and global bonds battered as inflation re-ignites. The Nifty shed another 0.7% on Saturday's session and the technical picture signals deeper volatility ahead with selling pressure intensifying. The family corpus posture remains bifurcated — hold crude-winners (upstream, defence, biofuels, renewables, pharma/IT exporters benefiting from rupee weakness) and continue reducing crude-and-rupee-losers (OMCs, aviation, quick-commerce) — but this week's earnings calendar (ONGC on 19 May, Titan on 22 May, UltraTech on 21 May) will be critical reality checks against the macro noise.

conviction.name: HDFC Bank
conviction.thesis: India's largest private-sector bank, finally past its post-merger digestion. Asset quality is at a multi-year best, the governance review is clearing, and the franchise's deposit-gathering machine is unmatched. DII buying confirmed HDFC Bank among top-10 most accumulated in Q4 — domestic institutions are adding, not fleeing.
catalysts: DII buying among top-10 in Q4 confirms institutional conviction
NIM stabilisation post HDFC Ltd merger absorption
Branch-led deposit growth re-accelerating
Retail credit cycle turning supportive in FY27
risks: Net interest margin pressure if bond yields surge further on crude-driven inflation
Credit costs in unsecured retail
Heavy index weight invites foreign-flow volatility — FII selling in Q4 a headwind

conviction.name: ICICI Bank
conviction.thesis: The best-run large bank in India by almost any operating metric — consistent ROA above 2%, conservative provisioning, a digital stack peers are still trying to replicate. FII selling in Q4 noted in top-10 lists but thesis is unbroken; we pay a premium happily for the quality gap.
catalysts: Industry-leading return on assets >2%
Cleaner book than every private peer
Fee income compounding at double digits
FII return to India likely to favour ICICI first among large banks once macro stabilises
risks: Valuation premium leaves less room for error
Slowing retail unsecured credit growth
Macroprudential tightening overhang if inflation resurges

conviction.name: State Bank of India
conviction.thesis: The flagship PSU bank is macro-pressured but fundamentally sound. Asset quality is at its cleanest in a decade, ROE has migrated above 16%, and it trades at roughly 1.5× book. SBI appeared in top-10 highest DII buying in Q4 — a powerful signal of domestic institutional support at current levels.
catalysts: Top-10 DII buying in Q4 — domestic institutions accumulating at these levels
Cleanest GNPA/NNPA ratios in 10+ years
Subsidiary value (SBI Cards, SBI Life, AMC) under-counted in price
Valuation gap vs private peers remains historically wide
risks: Government cross-currents (PSL targets, minority stake sales)
Treasury volatility as global yields surge to one-year highs
Slower fee-income growth than private peers

conviction.name: ITC
conviction.thesis: A cash-printing cigarette monopoly funding a steadily compounding FMCG business, plus hotels, paperboards, and agri. Near-zero debt, a 3.5%+ dividend yield, and a hotels demerger unlocking value. ITC Hotels Q4 PAT of ₹317 Cr confirms the hotels business is delivering; fully domestic revenue base is a complete hedge against rupee weakness at 96/USD.
catalysts: Hotels demerger value unlock — Q4 PAT ₹317 Cr, revenue ₹1,254 Cr confirms momentum
FMCG margins continuing to expand toward HUL's
Cigarette taxation cycle relatively benign
Rupee weakness irrelevant — fully domestic revenue base is the natural hedge
risks: Cigarette regulation / taxation surprises
FMCG rural demand recovery has been uneven
Tobacco-related ESG screens limit some institutional buying

conviction.name: Bharat Electronics
conviction.thesis: The crown jewel of Indian defence indigenisation. Order book over ₹75,000 Cr giving multi-year revenue visibility, ROCE above 25%, debt-free balance sheet. US-Iran combat fears, elevated border tensions, and global geopolitical re-armament converge into the most supportive backdrop for indigenous defence procurement in India's history.
catalysts: Defence capex growing at low-double digits in FY27 budget
Export orders compounding from a small base
Order book : revenue ratio above 3×
US-Iran conflict risk and border tensions elevating indigenous procurement urgency to multi-year highs
risks: Valuation multiple is the highest in its history
Order timing inherently lumpy
Margin pressure from competitive bidding

conviction.name: Power Finance Corp
conviction.thesis: Government-backed NBFC at the centre of India's power and renewables financing build-out. Trades at a single-digit P/E with a ~4% dividend yield, ROE in the high teens, and a loan book with vastly improved asset quality. Crude at $109 directly accelerates India's renewables financing pipeline — PFC is the primary conduit for that capital.
catalysts: Renewable energy financing the dominant growth driver
Asset quality at cyclical best
Re-rating potential as discom risk is repriced lower
Crude near $110 accelerates India's strategic push to renewables — more financing demand for PFC
risks: Concentration in power sector / discom credit risk
Tariff / regulatory interventions
Bond market volatility — global yields at one-year highs as crude-driven inflation bites

conviction.name: Oil & Natural Gas Corp
conviction.thesis: Brent at $109.26 — up 8% in a week on US-Iran combat fears — is the most direct earnings upgrade for ONGC. Q4/FY27 realisations will be materially higher. At P/E ~7.5× and P/B ~1×, with crude sustaining well above $100 and the windfall-tax regime better-understood, ONGC remains the cleanest crude-hedge in the portfolio. Results due 19 May — watch FY27 capex guidance and windfall tax commentary.
catalysts: Brent near $110 lifts realisations materially — FY27 earnings upgrade visible
Windfall tax regime more stable than feared
Gas price reform supporting earnings floor
Results on 19 May — key read on management confidence in sustained high crude environment
risks: Sharp crude correction if US-Iran geopolitical risk eases suddenly
Government windfall taxes can re-emerge at $100+ as political pressure mounts
Capex cycle pressure on free cash flow

conviction.name: Coforge
conviction.thesis: The bright spot in a battered IT sector. Deal wins are accelerating and the AI/cloud positioning is pulling clients from the giants. Rupee at 96/USD — having touched a record low before RBI intervention — provides a meaningful tailwind to reported rupee earnings, one of the few IT names where the macro shift works clearly in our favour.
catalysts: Deal wins outpacing Tier-1 IT
AI services book gaining real revenue traction
Cigniti acquisition synergies still ahead
INR near 96/USD adds ~200bps to rupee revenue growth
risks: IT sector sentiment remains poor — global inflation re-ignition threatens US client budgets
Concentration in BFSI vertical
Higher beta than large-cap IT in any global slowdown

conviction.name: Bajaj Auto
conviction.thesis: Export-led two-wheeler franchise with strong April sales momentum. Petrol price hikes will provide some near-term headwind to domestic two-wheeler volume sentiment, but Bajaj's export diversification and CNG/EV mix reduce sensitivity versus domestic-only peers significantly. The rupee at 96/USD is an incremental export revenue tailwind.
catalysts: Export tailwind back — 83% YoY growth in April
EV (Chetak) reaching meaningful volumes
CNG + 3W commercial cycle underway
Less domestic fuel-price sensitivity than Hero/TVS peers; INR tailwind on export revenues
risks: Petrol price hike dampens domestic two-wheeler demand near-term
EV margin profile still being established
Africa/LatAm currency exposure on exports

conviction.name: Reliance Industries
conviction.thesis: The default India mega-cap hardest hit in the top-10 m-cap destruction this week (Rs 3.12L Cr lost across top-10; Reliance hardest). Three engines remain: Jio (telecom), Reliance Retail (largest retailer), and O2C. Crude at $109 is mixed — supportive for O2C GRMs, but quick-commerce margin pressure and Jio capex intensity remain drags on ROE.
catalysts: Jio tariff hike cycle still has runway
Reliance Retail IPO talk persists as latent catalyst
New energy capex starting to produce revenue
O2C margin uplift as GRM widens with crude spike near $110
risks: Reliance hardest hit in top-10 m-cap destruction this week — FII selling confirmed
Quick-commerce competition pressuring retail margins
Conglomerate discount may persist longer than expected given capital intensity

longBets.name: Syrma SGS Technology
longBets.thesis: Top brokerage pick in Indian Electronics Manufacturing Services. The sector grew 24% CAGR FY19-24 and is forecast at 27% to FY29 on PLI schemes and China+1 supply-chain shifts. Margin expansion is structural as backward integration deepens. India's EMS market share is under 5% globally — it is heading higher. Near-term caution warranted on rupee at 96/USD raising imported component costs.
catalysts: FY26-28E revenue CAGR estimated at 29%, profit CAGR 44% by HDFC Sec
PLI scheme extension expected; budget tailwinds
Aerospace/defence/healthcare mix shift improving margins by 130bps
OSAT (semiconductor packaging) optionality being scoped
risks: Rupee at 96/USD raises imported component input costs materially
Cost competitiveness vs. China & Vietnam
Single-quarter margin volatility on input costs
Sector valuations under pressure — Kaynes crash a warning signal

longBets.name: Praj Industries
longBets.thesis: India's largest biofuel technology company. Crude at $109 is an unambiguous positive for biofuel economics — the E20 ethanol blending mandate becomes even more strategically imperative at high oil prices. Vijay Kedia's view that tourism could be India's next trillion-dollar story is an adjacent positive for aviation biofuels (SAF) that Praj is pioneering.
catalysts: E20 ethanol blending program scaling — crude above $100 accelerates urgency
SAF commercialisation underway globally; Praj is among very few Indian players
Order book recovering after temporary pause
High crude near $110 improves biofuel project economics dramatically
risks: Lumpy project order cycle
Recent quarterly loss reflects execution slippage
Sharp crude correction would dampen biofuel economics

longBets.name: Data Patterns (India)
longBets.thesis: Q4 revenue declined 13% YoY to ₹345 Cr — a significant miss confirming lumpy quarterly risk. The thesis has NOT broken: franchise quality, order pipeline, margin structure, and policy tailwind are all intact. US-Iran combat fears, border tensions, and the global re-armament cycle only deepen the indigenisation mandate. This is an entry window, not an exit.
catalysts: FY27 budget targeting 'Force Multipliers' (electronic warfare, drone swarms)
Order pipeline remains substantial despite quarterly lumpiness
Margin guidance 35–40% structurally unchanged
Tejas Mk1A and indigenous platform build-out multi-year
risks: Q4 revenue miss confirms lumpy quarterly execution — patience required
Valuation at 60×+ requires consistent delivery
Higher beta — 40%+ annualised volatility

longBets.name: MTAR Technologies
longBets.thesis: High-precision component supplier to defence, aerospace, civilian nuclear, and clean energy (fuel cells, electrolysers). Niche, hard-to-replicate manufacturing capabilities. The long-term thesis rests on being an irreplaceable precision parts supplier to multiple high-growth verticals simultaneously.
catalysts: Defence indigenisation orders compounding
Clean energy fuel-cell components scaling globally
Order book healthy across multiple verticals
Data-centre vertical opens new TAM
risks: Valuation at 165× P/E is the most stretched among peers
Margin profile choppy (10% ROE)
Single new-vertical bets carry execution risk

longBets.name: Astra Microwave Products
longBets.thesis: RF and microwave subsystems for radars, electronic warfare, and satellite payloads. Q3 FY26 profit jumped 96% QoQ; operating margins expanded to 31.7%. Geopolitical escalation globally — US-Iran conflict fears, India border tensions — are structural tailwinds for indigenous radar and EW procurement. Trades cheaper than peers.
catalysts: 12.4% rise in DRDO R&D funding for indigenous AESA radars
Q3 margins jumped to 31.7% on better mix
US-Iran conflict risk and border tensions structurally accelerating indigenous defence spending
Relatively cheaper vs Data Patterns on P/E basis
risks: Stock recently in technical downtrend
ROE at 10.5% lags Garden Reach (20%) and Data Patterns (13%)
Beta of 1.35 means sharper drawdowns in selloffs

longBets.name: KNR Constructions
longBets.thesis: Roads and highways EPC contractor with one of the cleanest balance sheets in the construction space. Government's NHAI awards remain a reliable pipeline, and KNR has consistently delivered above-industry execution. At 13.5× earnings, the valuation is genuinely undemanding for the quality on offer.
catalysts: NHAI award pipeline remains strong
Debt-free working capital management
Margin profile better than larger peers
Government infrastructure push unchanged despite crude headwinds
risks: Asset monetisation pace slower than hoped
Order inflows concentrated in NHAI
Construction cycle exposure to monsoon delays

longBets.name: Maharashtra Seamless
longBets.thesis: India's largest seamless pipe manufacturer for oil & gas, power, and infrastructure. Crude at $109+ directly accelerates domestic upstream capex — ONGC, Oil India, and private E&P companies will step up drilling and pipeline activity. Tata Steel's 147% PAT surge and SAIL's 47% growth confirm the domestic steel earnings cycle is healthy.
catalysts: Domestic oil & gas capex ramping — Brent near $110 is a direct demand driver
Strong steel sector earnings (Tata Steel PAT +147%, SAIL PAT +47%) signal healthy sector
Export market widening
Debt-free balance sheet; 14× P/E remains very undemanding
risks: Steel price volatility
Cyclical demand patterns
Concentration in oil & gas customer base

longBets.name: Ion Exchange (India)
longBets.thesis: Pioneer in water and wastewater treatment in India. ROCE of 27.5%, debt-equity 0.2, operating across municipal, industrial, and household water. Direct beneficiary of Jal Jeevan Mission and increasingly stringent industrial effluent norms. Fully domestic revenue — completely insulated from rupee weakness at 96/USD.
catalysts: Jal Jeevan Mission and similar government water programs
Industrial effluent compliance becoming mandatory
Premium consumer water purifier brand (Zero B)
Domestic revenue base — fully insulated from rupee weakness
risks: Project execution timing
Working capital intensity in EPC contracts
Smaller order sizes vs MNC competitors

highPromise.name: Computer Age Management Services
highPromise.thesis: A duopoly providing the picks-and-shovels for India's mutual fund industry. Q4 EBITDA margin expanded to 46.3%, profit grew 11%. As MF AUM compounds at 15%+ annually, CAMS rides that wave with operating leverage. NSE EGR trading commences 18 May — an incremental new fee pool from gold investment flowing through exchange platforms that CAMS is positioned to service.
catalysts: MF industry AUM growth structural at 15%+
New product wins (alt fund servicing, AIFs, EGRs)
NSE Electronic Gold Receipts platform launch 18 May — new fee pool catalyst
Best-in-class operating margins at 46%+
risks: Pricing pressure from large MFs
Regulatory caps on RTA fees
Concentration in top-5 AMC clients

highPromise.name: Wockhardt
highPromise.thesis: Posted a turnaround Q4 — ₹164 Cr profit versus a ₹45 Cr loss a year ago. The novel antibiotic pipeline (Zaynich, others) is reaching commercial inflection. Rupee weakness at 96/USD is an incremental tailwind for US export revenues. Speculative but asymmetric.
catalysts: Zaynich US launch progress
Specialty antibiotic pipeline maturing
Operating leverage as losses recede
Rupee near 96/USD incrementally favourable for US export revenues
risks: History of inconsistent execution
Balance sheet still recovering
Regulatory / FDA process risk

highPromise.name: Himachal Futuristic
highPromise.thesis: Optical fibre cable, 5G transmission gear, and a small but growing defence electronics order book. India's 5G + BharatNet + defence comms theme captured in one mid-cap name. Rupee weakness on imports is a headwind to watch on input costs.
catalysts: BharatNet phase 3 ramp
5G private network orders
Defence segment scaling from a small base
risks: Working-capital intensive
Order timing volatile
Margin pressure from raw material moves and rupee weakness on imports

highPromise.name: Suzlon Energy
highPromise.thesis: A fully restructured balance sheet, the largest order book in its history, and a wind capacity addition cycle just starting after years of dormancy. Brent near $110 is the most powerful political tailwind for accelerating India's domestic renewable energy push — the strategic urgency for energy self-sufficiency has never been higher. Suzlon is a direct beneficiary.
catalysts: Order book at multi-year highs
Net-debt-free for the first time in a decade
Wind add-back cycle in FY27–28
Crude near $110 — strongest political argument in years for domestic renewable acceleration
risks: Single-product, single-geography concentration
Execution risk on large orders
Investor base still partly speculative

highPromise.name: IdeaForge Technology
highPromise.thesis: Pure-play on Indian military and homeland-security drone procurement, an area where indigenisation policy is accelerating. Revenue inflection confirmed with a 7× YoY surge and return to profit. US-Iran combat fears and elevated border tensions are raising procurement urgency for surveillance and strike drone systems.
catalysts: Defence drone orders multi-year visible
Revenue inflection just confirmed
Limited domestic competition in UAV space
US-Iran conflict and border tensions elevating drone procurement urgency
risks: Lumpy order cycle
Tiny float, very volatile
Margin sustainability unproven at scale

watchClose.name: Tata Consultancy Services
watchClose.thesis: The bluest of blue chips, but caught in a sector-wide air pocket. FII selling in Q4 confirmed in top-10 lists. Rupee at 96/USD is a tailwind to reported INR revenues. Quality of business is unchanged; what has changed is the cyclical demand picture and a global inflation re-ignition that threatens IT budgets. We hold; we do not chase.
catalysts: Buyback / dividend yield supports floor
AI services adoption with marquee clients
INR near 96/USD meaningfully aids reported rupee earnings
risks: US client spending caution lingers — inflation fears re-igniting globally
FII selling confirmed in Q4 top-10 list
Premium multiple vs. growth trajectory

watchClose.name: Infosys
watchClose.thesis: Same story as TCS, slightly cheaper. Operating margins are pinched, but the franchise, balance sheet and capital return habit are intact. Rupee tailwind at 96/USD is supportive. Not a sell, just not yet a buy.
catalysts: AI / cloud deal momentum
Margin recovery as discretionary spend returns
Steady buyback cadence
risks: Global IT budget compression continues — inflation resurgence is not helping
Onsite cost pressure
Sector de-rating not yet over

watchClose.name: Hindustan Unilever
watchClose.thesis: Volume growth has returned and the FY27 outlook is brighter — but at ~55× earnings, you are paying for a perfect recovery. Crude at $109 raises palm oil and packaging input cost pressures. Trim, don't add.
catalysts: Rural demand recovery gathering pace
Premiumisation across categories
Margin recovery once palm oil cools
risks: Valuation leaves no room for misses
Quick-commerce reshaping distribution economics
Crude at $109 raises palm oil / packaging input cost pressure

watchClose.name: Asian Paints
watchClose.thesis: The franchise is real, the brand is real — but Birla Opus remains the most credible threat to the moat in twenty years. Until we see how share-loss settles, holding is the right answer; adding is not. Crude at $109 also raises raw material (TiO2, petrochemical derivatives) cost pressures.
catalysts: Decorative volume growth recovery
Industrial paints scaling
Margin defence playbook intact
risks: Birla Opus competitive intensity
Multi-quarter market share concession likely
Crude at $109 raises petrochemical input costs

watchClose.name: Larsen & Toubro
watchClose.thesis: Guided FY27 revenue growth lower on Middle East disruptions — and Brent at $109 with active US-Iran combat fears means West Asia tensions are worsening, not easing. The long-cycle infra story is unchanged; the near-term margin and order-timing headwinds are real and have intensified. Hold; let the dust settle.
catalysts: Domestic infra & defence order pipeline intact
Hyderabad campus / IT services value
Middle East order book recovery once tensions ease
risks: West Asia exposure to conflict risk — US-Iran combat fears are an acute escalation
Margin guidance has been reset down
Capex slowdown if elections shift policy

watchClose.name: Bharti Airtel
watchClose.thesis: Best-positioned in a duopoly, with strong ARPU momentum and Africa optionality. But the stock has already priced much of the next two years of tariff hikes. We hold what we have; we don't add aggressively here.
catalysts: ARPU compounding into ₹240+
5G monetisation begins
Africa cash flow turning material
risks: Capex demands remain heavy
Regulatory / spectrum costs
Premium valuation vs. global telecom peers

trimAvoid.name: Trent
trimAvoid.thesis: Zudio is a brilliant business; Trent at this price is a brilliant business priced as if it cannot stumble. Single-month drawdowns of 22% in such names are reminders that valuation matters. Trim into strength.
catalysts: Store rollout still aggressive
Brand strength in value fashion
risks: P/E above 100× is structurally hard to defend
Saturation in Tier-1 cities arriving
Any same-store-sales miss is asymmetrically punished

trimAvoid.name: Avenue Supermarts
trimAvoid.thesis: A great business with a slowing growth equation. Quick-commerce is reshaping the urban grocery basket faster than DMart's store-led model can respond. The valuation still assumes the old growth trajectory; the new one is materially lower.
catalysts: Steady store additions
Best-in-class working capital
risks: Quick-commerce eating high-frequency baskets
Same-store-sales-growth slowing
Multiple still 80–90× earnings

trimAvoid.name: Nestle India
trimAvoid.thesis: An exceptional brand portfolio at a price that demands exceptional growth — which has not been delivered. Volume growth has been mid-single-digit; the multiple is double that of global staples. Hold a small position at most.
catalysts: Pricing power intact
Distribution expansion in smaller towns
risks: Valuation vs. growth gap is the largest in years
Royalty hike overhang reappears periodically
Premium FMCG demand softening

trimAvoid.name: Eternal (Zomato)
trimAvoid.thesis: Blinkit is genuinely interesting; the valuation prices in it being interesting forever. Despite appearing in top-10 DII buying in Q4, crude at $109 raises last-mile delivery costs materially and the path to durable profitability is narrower than the share price suggests. Avoid.
catalysts: Blinkit GMV scaling rapidly
Going-out / events business optionality
risks: Quick-commerce profitability still unproven at scale
Crude at $109 raises delivery economics pressure materially
Capex war intensifying with Swiggy and Reliance

trimAvoid.name: Titan Company
trimAvoid.thesis: Titan's near-term outlook remains under pressure. Gold in USD fell 2.5% to $4,562/oz but at rupee near 96/USD, gold in INR terms remains near all-time highs, keeping demand elasticity negative. Import duty tightening adds further margin pressure. Watch jewellery volume guidance from the 22 May results before reconsidering.
catalysts: Brand strength and store rollout intact long-term
Non-jewellery categories (watches, eyewear) provide some offset
risks: Gold import duty tightening squeezes jewellery margins and volumes
Gold price in INR terms near all-time highs despite USD pullback
Valuation premium under threat if earnings estimates cut on 22 May

trimAvoid.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corp
trimAvoid.thesis: Brent at $109.26 with the rupee at record lows near 96/USD is a double-body-blow for HPCL. The fuel price hike announced was 'not enough to offset all losses' per market reporting, and further hikes face political resistance. Avoid while crude stays elevated and geopolitical risk persists.
catalysts: Refining margins could widen if product cracks hold
Government subsidy backstop in extremis
risks: Marketing margin squeeze as Brent near $110 — hike insufficient per analysts
Government resistance to full retail price pass-through
Rupee at 96/USD amplifies crude import cost — double squeeze

sectors.name: Private Banking
sectors.note: Asset quality at a decadal best; DII buying confirmed HDFC Bank and ICICI in top-10 most accumulated in Q4. FII selling is a headwind but valuations remain reasonable on the leaders. Rate-cut cycle essentially done.

sectors.name: PSU Banking
sectors.note: SBI in top-10 DII buying in Q4 — domestic institutions adding conviction. Cleanest books in years, single-digit P/Es. Macro pressure (crude + weak INR) is temporary; subsidiary value remains a multi-year unlock.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: INR near 96/USD record low is a meaningful rupee earnings tailwind; partially offsets demand caution from US clients. India missed AI leadership per one bearish headline but IT franchises intact. FII selling in TCS/Infosys confirmed in Q4 top-10 lists.

sectors.name: FMCG
sectors.note: Recovery underway but priced into most names. Crude near $110 raises palm oil and packaging input costs — margin pressure returning. ITC remains the best-positioned given domestic revenue base and hotels demerger.

sectors.name: Auto
sectors.note: Petrol/diesel price hikes a near-term headwind to domestic two-wheeler demand; export-heavy players (Bajaj) more insulated; EV mix growing. Fuel hikes 'not enough to offset all losses' signals more pain ahead for domestic demand.

sectors.name: Pharma
sectors.note: US generics cycle stable, domestic chronic therapy compounding. Rupee at/near 96/USD is a structural export earnings booster — most direct sector beneficiary of INR weakness. Wockhardt turnaround adds small-cap optionality.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: Rate cuts flowing through; inventory cycle supportive in top-7 cities. Crude has limited direct impact on domestic residential demand. InvIT regulatory easing (Sebi allowing extra debt for capex) is a positive adjacency.

sectors.name: Capital Goods / Infra
sectors.note: Domestic order books healthy; Middle East execution risk has worsened with US-Iran combat fears. L&T guidance reset and West Asia exposure are caution flags. NHAI and domestic infra remain sound.

sectors.name: Energy / Oil & Gas
sectors.note: Brent near $110 is a strong earnings upgrade for upstream (ONGC results 19 May key). OMCs facing double-squeeze (crude cost + rupee weakness, fuel hike insufficient) — bifurcate sharply: own upstream, avoid downstream.

sectors.name: Defence
sectors.note: US-Iran conflict fears and elevated border tensions accelerate indigenous procurement urgency. Geopolitical backdrop is the most supportive in years. Data Patterns Q4 miss is lumpy quarterly execution, not thesis-breaking.

sectors.name: Renewables
sectors.note: Crude near $110 is the strongest political argument in years for accelerating domestic renewables — strategic energy self-sufficiency imperative rising sharply. PFC and Suzlon are primary beneficiaries. Wind and solar capacity addition urgency at multi-year high.

sectors.name: Quick-Commerce / Internet
sectors.note: Capex war intensifying; crude near $110 raises last-mile delivery costs materially. Eternal (Zomato) appeared in DII top-10 buying but path to profit is narrowing, not widening. Delivery economics under structural pressure.

whispers.text: Brent holding near $109 through the weekend — up ~8% on the week — as US-Iran combat fears remain in markets. This is no longer a fear trade; markets are pricing active conflict disruption to supply. The bifurcation between crude-winners (ONGC, upstream, biofuels, renewables, pharma exporters) and crude-losers (HPCL, aviation, two-wheelers, quick-commerce delivery) must be maintained with conviction into next week.

The rupee breached 96/USD for the first time on record before RBI intervention. India is scrambling to steady the rupee as the oil shock bites, per ET Markets. A structurally weak rupee changes the earnings calculus significantly — IT, pharma, and upstream exporters win; EMS, electronics importers, and crude-dependent sectors lose. Watch RBI FX reserve drawdown pace and any SEBI/CBDT regulatory easing for foreign investors.
whispers.src: RBI intervention reports; ET Markets FX desk

whispers.text: Global bonds are being battered as crude-driven inflation spooks investors across the US, Europe, and Japan. US stocks down on mounting inflation worries, yields at one-year highs, Dow crashed 500 points. For India, the rate-cut cycle is firmly paused, cost-of-capital environment no longer supportive, and any high-multiple stock faces additional compression risk. The macro is a headwind for the quality-at-any-price approach.
whispers.src: ET Markets; Bloomberg; Powell Fed statements

whispers.text: Nifty at 23,643 — down from the 52-week high of 26,373 and only 6.5% above the 52-week low of 22,183. The 'fragile trend flagging deeper volatility' per ET Markets technicians is a signal to keep cash dry, maintain high-quality bias, and not average down into deteriorating technicals. 5 macro factors will drive D-Street action this week: crude, rupee, global yields, FII flows, and the earnings calendar.

Tata Steel Q4 PAT soared 147% YoY to ₹2,965 Cr, SAIL PAT surged 47% to ₹1,835 Cr. These are significant positive earnings surprises confirming that India's commodity and manufacturing earnings cycle is healthy — the bearish macro narrative overstates the fundamental damage. JSW Steel 13-fold PAT surge adds to the picture. Maharashtra Seamless is the most direct portfolio beneficiary.

US-Iran combat fears, elevated India border tensions, and the global re-armament cycle are converging into the most supportive geopolitical backdrop for Indian defence indigenisation ever. BEL, Data Patterns, Astra Microwave, MTAR, and IdeaForge are all beneficiaries. The Q4 quarterly noise at Data Patterns is irrelevant against this structural backdrop — patience is the edge here.

whispers.text: Q4 data shows Reliance, TCS, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank among top FII sellers while SBI, Groww, Eternal and HDFC Bank simultaneously saw highest DII buying in value terms. This divergence — foreign capital exiting and domestic capital absorbing — is a classic Indian market pattern near lows. History suggests DII-dominated accumulation zones have been better entry points than FII-led highs.
